{"judgments": [
{"clause_id":"c181","reasoning_cat1":"'Lowest responsible bidder', 'a manner reasonably likely to attract prospective bidders' and 'financially responsible' are undefined qualitative tests governing a mandatory bidding regime.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 8.4 imposes a different sealed-bid regime for concessions and Section 12.13 another for bonds, while Section 12.20(b) overrides bidding for bonds sold to signatory agencies.","prob_cat1":0.30,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c182","reasoning_cat1":"An objective exemption identified by counterparty; nothing evaluative.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 1.5 and 3.9(b) on employing other governmental agencies.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c183","reasoning_cat1":"'The public exigency requires the immediate delivery' is a wholly evaluative and self-judged trigger for waiving competitive bidding.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 10.4's emergency machinery uses a different and more formal trigger, but the two operate in separate spheres.","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c184","reasoning_cat1":"'Only one source of supply is available' is a factual test, though 'available' has some elasticity.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the rest of Section 14.9's waiver list.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c185","reasoning_cat1":"'Of a technical nature' and 'necessary in order to assure standardization ... in the public interest' pile three open-ended judgments into one waiver ground.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the other waiver grounds in Section 14.9.","prob_cat1":0.27,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c186","reasoning_cat1":"'Services ... of a specialized or professional nature' is the vaguest item in the waiver list and sits at its end, functioning as a catch-all that could swallow the bidding rule.","reasoning_cat2":"It undercuts the mandatory sealed-bid requirement in the same section's opening sentence, a tension internal to Section 14.9.","prob_cat1":0.33,"prob_cat2":0.19},
{"clause_id":"c187","reasoning_cat1":"'Pay the premiums therefore' misuses 'therefore' for 'therefor', and 'loss of revenue from any cause whatsoever' is a sweeping but permissive phrase.","reasoning_cat2":"Its subordination to bond agreements ties it to Section 12.6's insurance covenants, consistently.","prob_cat1":0.20,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c188","reasoning_cat1":"'As soon as practical' (for 'practicable') and 'no personal interest direct or indirect' are soft, and the section sets no audit deadline at all.","reasoning_cat2":"Sections 14.11(b), (c) and New York's Section 640 add overlapping audit rights, which coexist rather than conflict.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c189","reasoning_cat1":"'All other papers, things or property of the commission' is a sweeping catch-all appended to an enumerated list of records.","reasoning_cat2":"New York's Section 640 channels this right to the state comptroller, and Section 15.1(q) reserves separate congressional disclosure rights.","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.21},
{"clause_id":"c190","reasoning_cat1":"A short provision subjecting the Commission's transactions to GAO audit under comptroller general rules; definite in terms.","reasoning_cat2":"It treats the Commission like a federal instrumentality even though Section 15.1(m) provides that for stated purposes 'the commission shall not be considered a Federal agency', and Section 14.11(a) already provides for independent audit.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c191","reasoning_cat1":"'Refuse to give all require assistance' is ungrammatical — plainly a dropped 'd' from 'required' — in a clause that imposes automatic forfeiture of office.","reasoning_cat2":"It parallels the forfeiture sanction in Section 14.8(b) but applies without any wilfulness requirement, an inconsistency in the compact's disciplinary standards.","prob_cat1":0.40,"prob_cat2":0.23},
{"clause_id":"c192","reasoning_cat1":"A plain annual-reporting duty plus a discretionary publication power.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 3.6(f) and 14.4(c).","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c193","reasoning_cat1":"A bare permissive introduction.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 12.20(c) and 14.1(a)(2).","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c194","reasoning_cat1":"'Preliminary expenses such as' introduces an illustrative list whose outer boundary is undefined.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 12.2 and 12.20(c) on funding purposes.","prob_cat1":0.18,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c195","reasoning_cat1":"'Necessary or convenient' is soft but the advancing power itself is plain.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 12.20(c) and 14.13(b) on repayment.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c196","reasoning_cat1":"'For benefits received or to be received' is broad but the payment power is permissive.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 4.3 and 11.4 on benefit-based charges.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c197","reasoning_cat1":"Repayment terms are left entirely to later agreement, which leaves the obligation indefinite but transparently so.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 12.1 and 12.20(a); no conflicting provision found.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c198","reasoning_cat1":"'Includes but is not limited to' introduces a catch-all, and the exclusion 'other than property of a signatory party and any property held ... in connection with a diversion authorized by a United States Supreme Court decree' is awkwardly conjoined and hard to parse.","reasoning_cat2":"It must be squared with Section 3.5(c)'s bar on Commission jurisdiction over decree-related facilities and with Section 14.15's separate conveyance machinery.","prob_cat1":0.33,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c199","reasoning_cat1":"A clear choice-of-procedure rule with an express fallback to state condemnation law.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 15.1(m) and 15.1(p) on the Commission's federal/state posture, though those complicate which law is 'applicable'.","prob_cat1":0.15,"prob_cat2":0.19},
{"clause_id":"c200","reasoning_cat1":"A flat allocation of liability for condemnation awards; nothing to construe.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 12.3 and 12.20(a) on the parties' non-liability.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c201","reasoning_cat1":"'Necessary or convenient to the effectuation of the authorized purposes' is soft, but the provision only authorises conveyances.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 14.1(a)(5) and 14.14.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c202","reasoning_cat1":"'Authorized and empowered ... to grant and convey ... upon the commission's request' leaves genuinely unclear whether a political subdivision must convey when asked or merely may.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 14.14(a) provides a condemnation route for property 'already devoted to a public use', which suggests conveyance here is voluntary — but the 'upon request' phrasing points the other way.","prob_cat1":0.29,"prob_cat2":0.22},
{"clause_id":"c203","reasoning_cat1":"'Shall not in any event exceed the expenditure required to serve the public convenience and necessity' is an undefined ceiling on relocation costs.","reasoning_cat2":"It interacts with Section 14.14(a)'s public-utility carve-out, which turns on whether the facility 'is to be relocated or replaced'.","prob_cat1":0.30,"prob_cat2":0.22},
{"clause_id":"c204","reasoning_cat1":"'Subject to such reasonable conditions as the highway department ... may require' is a familiar reasonableness qualifier on an otherwise clear grant.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 14.14 and 14.15; state highway authority is preserved rather than displaced.","prob_cat1":0.18,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c205","reasoning_cat1":"'Punishable as may be provided by statute of any of the signatory parties within which the offense is committed' mixes 'any' with a single-jurisdiction test, and the default $50–$1,000 penalty is left to be 'fixed by the court'.","reasoning_cat2":"It attaches criminal-type consequences to rules whose validity depends on the filing requirement in Section 14.2(a) and to orders reviewable under Section 5.4.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c206","reasoning_cat1":"'Only to the extent and subject to the procedures prescribed by law generally with respect to officers, agents and employees of the government of the United States' imports an entire federal liability regime by reference, with no indication which statutes are meant.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 15.1(m) provides the Commission is not a federal agency for the Federal Tort Claims Act statutes it cites, so the borrowed regime and the disclaimer point in opposite directions.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.42},
{"clause_id":"c207","reasoning_cat1":"A short savings clause; 'affecting or intending to affect or in any way to interfere with' is redundant but directionally clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Article 10's withdrawal permits, Section 4.2(b)'s diversion bar and Section 14.14(a)'s power to condemn 'riparian rights' all plainly affect riparian rights under state law.","prob_cat1":0.21,"prob_cat2":0.41},
{"clause_id":"c208","reasoning_cat1":"'Amendments and supplements ... to implement the purposes thereof' limits amendment by an undefined purposive test, and unanimity is required.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 15.1(q) reserves to Congress the unilateral 'right to alter, amend, or repeal this Act', and Section 1.4 recognises unilateral federal modification — hard to square with a unanimity rule.","prob_cat1":0.20,"prob_cat2":0.35},
{"clause_id":"c209","reasoning_cat1":"'It is the legislative intent that the provisions of such compact be reasonably and liberally construed' is itself a construction directive that parties fight over, and 'reasonably' pulls against 'liberally'.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 15.1(t) provides that invalidity of Section 1.4 ends US participation altogether, which is the opposite of the general severability declared here.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.38},
{"clause_id":"c210","reasoning_cat1":"'Thirty days after the enactment of concurring legislation' is a definite trigger, and the execution mechanics are specific.","reasoning_cat2":"The concurring state acts and Section 15.3 each say 'this act shall take effect immediately', which sits awkwardly with the thirty-day rule.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.28},
{"clause_id":"c211","reasoning_cat1":"An introductory conditions clause tied to Section 1.4; no operative term of its own.","reasoning_cat2":"It subordinates the whole compact to the reservations that follow, several of which override named compact sections.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c212","reasoning_cat1":"'Beyond the planning stage' is an undefined threshold, and the carve-out for 'a project for which State supplied funds only will be used' turns on a funding characterisation that may change over time.","reasoning_cat2":"Requiring an Act of Congress for every project cuts deeply into the Commission's operational powers in Articles 3 through 9 and its plan under Section 13.1, a whole-instrument tension the compact never resolves.","prob_cat1":0.32,"prob_cat2":0.43},
{"clause_id":"c213","reasoning_cat1":"The text reads 'impose any change for water withdrawals or diversions' where 'charge' is plainly meant — a mechanical error in the operative verb of the restriction.","reasoning_cat2":"It cuts down Section 3.7's rate power and overlaps Section 3.5(b) and Section 11.3, and its own proviso subordinates it to Section 1.4, leaving a layered set of qualifications.","prob_cat1":0.48,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c214","reasoning_cat1":"'The executive powers of the President in the event of a national emergency' is an undefined and contested body of authority invoked without limit.","reasoning_cat2":"It overlaps Section 10.4's emergency machinery and Section 15.1(s)'s presidential override without saying how they interact.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c215","reasoning_cat1":"'Shall serve at the pleasure of the President' is unambiguous on its own terms.","reasoning_cat2":"The compact's own endnote records that this provision and Section 2.2 ('during the term of office of the President') were inconsistent until 1997 — an expressly acknowledged internal conflict.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.57},
{"clause_id":"c216","reasoning_cat1":"'Impairing or in any manner affecting the applicability to all Federal funds budgeted and appropriated for use by the commission' is missing its object — the applicability of what? — so the sentence does not parse.","reasoning_cat2":"It bears on Sections 12.20 and 13.3(c) concerning federal contributions, and the WRDA endnote adds further funding directives.","prob_cat1":0.43,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c217","reasoning_cat1":"'Are or may continued to be free or exempt' is ungrammatical (a dropped 'continue'), in the operative comparison that defines the exemption's scope.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 12.8 exempts Commission bonds from 'all taxation by or under authority of any of the signatory parties', and the federal government is a signatory party under Section 1.2(h) — a direct clash this paragraph is trying to fix.","prob_cat1":0.36,"prob_cat2":0.40},
{"clause_id":"c218","reasoning_cat1":"A short and unmistakable disclaimer of federal obligation, legal or moral.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 12.1 and 12.3, which limit recourse to Commission revenues.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c219","reasoning_cat1":"'Pledged only to the extent that the respective agencies shall from time to time agree' converts a pledge into a discretion, but says so openly.","reasoning_cat2":"It expressly overrides Section 11.5's pledge of technical and administrative services, and sits against Section 15.2(b)'s directive that agencies 'shall cooperate with and furnish appropriate assistance'.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.35},
{"clause_id":"c220","reasoning_cat1":"'In excess of eight hours in any workday or forty hours in any workweek, as the case may be' leaves the overtime trigger genuinely uncertain, and the string of statutory citations contains an unclosed parenthesis.","reasoning_cat2":"It attaches wage conditions to Commission contracting that Section 14.9's bidding regime does not mention.","prob_cat1":0.29,"prob_cat2":0.17},
{"clause_id":"c221","reasoning_cat1":"A short threshold rule incorporating a named statute; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"The $10,000 figure matches Section 14.9's construction threshold but not its $2,500 supplies threshold, a minor mismatch.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.19},
{"clause_id":"c222","reasoning_cat1":"The paragraph says federal water-pollution functions are not limited by the compact and then provides that the exercise of those functions 'shall not limit the authority of the commission' — a circular pair in which neither yields.","reasoning_cat2":"It must be read with Sections 5.2, 5.4 and 5.5, which already divide pollution authority between the Commission and the signatories, leaving three overlapping regimes.","prob_cat1":0.38,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c223","reasoning_cat1":"A one-sentence disapplication of a named section; clear.","reasoning_cat2":"It carves federally operated facilities out of Section 8.4's mandatory concession bidding, an exception the reader must find in Part II.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.22},
{"clause_id":"c224","reasoning_cat1":"A dense list of statutory citations, but its operative statement — the Commission is not a federal agency for those purposes — is definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 14.18 makes the Commission liable in tort only as federal officers and employees are, which is difficult to operate once the Federal Tort Claims Act statutes are disapplied.","prob_cat1":0.17,"prob_cat2":0.36},
{"clause_id":"c225","reasoning_cat1":"The parenthetical exclusions ('advisors, and personnel employed by the United States member under direct Federal appropriation') are clumsily punctuated but intelligible.","reasoning_cat2":"It coexists with Sections 14.5 and 15.1(r), which permit federal compensation of the US member and advisor.","prob_cat1":0.20,"prob_cat2":0.19},
{"clause_id":"c226","reasoning_cat1":"A short non-enlargement clause with no evaluative term.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 11.1(c) and 15.1(s)1, which preserve rather than enlarge federal agency authority.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.17},
